dict.string:
Captain Polliwog 0.3 (alpha)
The JavaScript engine is on. This build turns on the PowerPC baseline JIT, which had been built but not shipped. JavaScript is about twice as fast as before, and up to five times on the kind of code a charting library writes.
Faster everywhere else too. A fix to our copy of GCC removed a dead register save and restore from 15,928 of WebCore's functions. WebCore now exports 6,917 symbols instead of 73,627, which removed 5,484 stubs that stood in front of calls it makes to itself. Speedometer 3.1 on a PowerBook G4: 0.520, from 0.271 two days ago.
Video can be handed to a real player. QuickTime's H.264 decoder is the slowest part of watching anything on these machines. Right-click a video, use the green button on it, the View menu or the Share menu, and it opens in VLC or MPlayer instead, which decode with AltiVec. The stream goes through the browser's own networking, so seeking works and sites that refuse Tiger's TLS are reachable.
Full screen works. It was off twice over: WebKit's own preference for it, and the missing unprefixed requestFullscreen() that modern players look for.
Nothing plays by itself. A video that starts on its own is the whole processor on a G4. Pages that call play() from script are now stopped until you ask. Preferences has a switch for it.
Say when something is wrong. There is a Send Feedback window now, and an About window that says what this is and which build you are on.
Known: Charts-chartjs is still slower than PowerFox. There is no Media Source Extensions, so YouTube will only offer 360p. Tiger and G3 support is not in this build.

Captain Polliwog 0.3.1 (alpha)
Welcome aboard. The first time it opens, the Captain introduces himself and offers to bring your Safari bookmarks across, to become your default browser, and to recommend a media player. The video page only recommends VLC on a Mac that can run it - its PowerPC build needs AltiVec, which a G3 does not have - and says so honestly on one that cannot. You can finish it later: untick "Don't show this again". Preferences > General has Run Setup Again.
Scrolling speed. Preferences > General > Scrolling: Slow, Medium, Fast or Very fast. Slow is the new default. The trackpad on these PowerBooks reports its own accelerated movement, and the old setting was moving pages more than a screen and a half a second.
Check for Updates says what it means. "Up to date" is now a plain answer with the version and build, instead of a window with an empty box in it and a progress bar running under its buttons.
The About window. The Cytrus Software logo is the real one now, and the icons are the right way up.
Known: Charts-chartjs is still slower than PowerFox. There is no Media Source Extensions, so YouTube only offers 360p - use the green Play in VLC button for a smoother picture. Tiger and G3 support is not in this build.

Captain Polliwog 0.3.2 (alpha)
The modern engine now runs on Tiger. Until now, Mac OS X 10.4 fell back to the WebKit the system shipped with in 2005, and modern sites had no chance. This build carries a second engine built for 10.4 and a G3, and picks whichever your Mac can run when it opens. It renders pages on a 500MHz Pismo.
Tiger's CoreText turned out to take font sizes as a different kind of number than Leopard's, which is why every earlier attempt stopped on the first line of styled text. Three of its calls differ that way.
What is off on Tiger: WebGL, Web Audio and game controllers. Tiger has nothing to build them on. Everything else is the same engine the Leopard build uses.
The download is larger because both engines are in it.
YouTube no longer quits the browser. YouTube's main script contains one function large enough that compiling it produced about 50MB of PowerPC code, and a PowerPC jump instruction reaches 32MB. The engine noticed and stopped the app, which looked like a page of grey boxes that never finished loading. The compiler now leaves a function that big to the interpreter and compiles everything else as before.
The status bar can tell you what a page is doing. Turn on Show Page Activity in the View menu. The bottom left then says what is being contacted, how many of the page's pieces have arrived, what it is still fetching after the page looks finished, and how long the page's own scripts held the browser up. Off unless you ask for it.
Smaller things. The setup assistant no longer counts QuickTime Player as a video player, since every Mac has it and it is the decoder the browser already uses - it now offers VLC as it was meant to. One call the browser made on every page only existed on Leopard, which would have raised on Tiger.

Captain Polliwog 0.3.3 (alpha)
Tiger stops losing the browser on ordinary pages. On Mac OS X 10.4 this would start, render, and then disappear - on YouTube, on MacRumors, on most pages with a video. Three separate reasons, and none of them was a crash: each was a function the browser asked 10.4 for that 10.4 has never had. Because those are looked up only when first used, the application always started, and always died later, on whichever page reached one first.
The 10.5 headers this is built against rename open, close, mmap and mktime to conformance variants Tiger's system library does not have. ICU wanted mktime, which is any page with a date on it. libxml2 wanted a zlib function Leopard added, for reading compressed files off disk - something a browser never does, so that is simply gone now. And the C++ runtime asked the system for the function that unwinds a thrown exception, which on 10.4 would have ended the browser the first time anything threw.
Six QuickTime names finish the list. WebKit looks them up by name and treats a miss as fatal; Tiger ships QuickTime 7.0.4 and six of them came later. So on 10.4 the browser did not fail to play a video - it stopped, on the first page holding one.
Text on Tiger is laid out at the size the page asked for. Headings came out as an unreadable smear with every letter on top of the last. 10.4's CoreGraphics answers glyph widths in its own units whatever size it is given: the same line at 11, 22, 44 and 88 pixels all measured 22 pixels wide. Lucida Grande was the one font it got right, which is why menus and toolbars looked fine above headlines that did not. Tiger now measures through CoreText, which gets every font right.
Open in VLC opens VLC again. It was passing an option the PowerPC build of VLC does not have, so VLC printed its usage and exited before drawing a window. Nothing reported it, because starting VLC had succeeded - it started, and chose to leave. The button also used to fail silently when a page's video could not be handed over at all; now it says so.
Smaller things. ICU, libxml2, libxslt, SQLite and the font sanitiser are all rebuilt. On Leopard nothing here should look different - every one of these was a 10.4 problem - so if it does, that is worth reporting.

Captain Polliwog 0.3.4
New
- A sidebar for your tabs, on Shift-Command-L. Favicons, titles, and a close cross on the row you are pointing at. - A Reader button appears in the address bar when a page is worth reading that way, and not when it is not. - A history window on Command-Y, searchable, with the last two thousand pages. - Close every tab and you land on Top Sites and your favourites rather than an empty window. If you would rather not have Top Sites, there is now a switch for it in Preferences. - The keyboard shortcuts from Safari: Command-1 to 9 for tabs, Command-0, Command-Shift-[ and ] to move between them, Control-Tab, Command-O to open a file, Command-J for downloads, and a Develop menu with Option-Command-U for the page source.
Fixed
- A crash while reading webmail. Style invalidation walked a stack of ancestor elements and, in a case Gmail produces, popped it past the bottom and read an element that was not there. Found by leaving pages running for ten minutes at a time; the browser had been closing them too quickly to notice. - Cookies on Tiger. The engine asked for a property of a cookie that 10.4 has never had, which stopped it partway through the list, so whether a cookie reached a page depended on where it happened to sit. This does not give Tiger HttpOnly protection - that system cannot represent the flag at all - but it no longer loses cookies over it. - The address bar is the same colour as the rest of the toolbar again, on both Tiger and Leopard, including the strip behind the text while you are typing in it. - The offer to download VLC for PowerPC works again. VideoLAN moved that file behind two redirects to a mirror; it now comes from the master host directly.
Faster
- About six per cent on Speedometer 3.1, from four fixes to JavaScriptCore's baseline JIT: arithmetic profiling that was being written and never read, inline cache sizes that were wrong for this processor, the "in" operator compiled properly for every kind of array, and a call into libm that was corrupting our own stack frame. - The engine is now chosen by your processor as well as your system, so a G4 gets the build made for a G4.
Known
- You cannot sign in to a Google account. Google's sign-in needs BigInt, which this engine does not have and cannot be given without a newer one. Work on that newer engine is under way and is a long road. - Some large sites use a lot of memory - Vimeo can reach a gigabyte on a page left open. Keep an eye on it if your Mac has 512MB or less.
